study.question: After the local gains from coarse linear and quadratic ordinal summaries, does replacing the incumbent redundant fifth match summary with a coarse cubic contrast improve full-population click AUC at fixed learned capacity, beyond a scrambled contrast and an eligibility-matched duplicate?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g0-r0013-block_task reaches 0.66501112 click AUC and g0-r0014-curvature_task reaches 0.66560707, above its same-capacity duplicate-linear 0.66475357 and scrambled-curvature 0.66479411 controls. These single-seed observations motivate an unresolved higher-order coarse-position signal, not a general claim that more moments help. The incumbent g0-r0017-available_norm is 0.66586052, but its fifth coefficient is just a norm-rescaled copy of the first centered target-match direction. Coarse changes orthogonal to constants, linear and quadratic block ranks are invisible to all five fixed summary coefficients (learned base compression may still observe them). A block-constant cubic residual can expose such changes without adding learned capacity. Its useful ordering information should beat both a common-gate norm-matched match duplicate and a scrambled cubic residual. Contradictory trajectories matter: direct compressed task queries g0-r0006-compressed_task scored 0.65919424 below the stronger source 0.66064694; ordered target-match-by-block interaction g0-r0016-joint_ordered scored 0.66564377 below duplicate-match 0.66573908; latest local block-energy balancing scored 0.66552831 below reversed 0.66582195 and global 0.66586052. Thus neither task conditioning, additional directions, nor locally balanced energy is uniformly beneficial. This study tests a different block-constant direction; it does not reassert those failed explanations. Baseline auxiliary AUCs (cart 0.84907, fav 0.86490, buy 0.87018) exceed incumbent auxiliary AUCs (0.78722, 0.78571, 0.78806); click gains do not establish improvement on all tasks.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text lines271-282 supports retaining unnormalized target-conditioned pooling and cautions that sequence modeling is not automatically beneficial. We retain the adapted scorer; replace one separate signed residual summary with a fixed orthogonal coarse ordinal coefficient. This is not exact DIN reproduction or an originality claim.

Pinned benchmark forward175-200 flattens event embeddings with user/context, then learned tokenization and interaction. Here fixed masked projections retain selected sequence information before task adapters while the inherited compressed target-conditioned pooling remains. No flatten tokenizer or UniMixing blocks are adopted. Benchmark code equivalence to the original paper has not been verified.

Cached primary benchmark section2.3 lines9,17,21,39 describes heterogeneous task tokens, flattening, sparse filtering and sequential transduction. This local comparison changes only a fixed supplemental coefficient, with none of these full architectures imported. Original-method full-paper detail is unavailable for the retrieved industry references; novelty remains unverified.

Actual candidate source SHA256 2f710c8db0ad978fb51d0206205ddeb22af5c115f8ae8c624a0a7b5bc5f06f5a verified before editing. The prior fifth matches the first match direction at a different norm. The new fifth instead lies in the coarse block-constant complement of the first four directions on common support. All learned components and their allocation/initialization remain identical.

inherited_components: Full frozen host recipe and adapted DIN field/action embeddings, unnormalized local activation and four towers
g2 source uniform click / feedback-stratified auxiliary ten-block compression and primary-owned item/scorer gradients
Task-specific zero-output-initialized residual adapters; first four match/local-ordinal/coarse-linear/coarse-quadratic summaries and match counts
Incumbent fifth norm and availability expression retained exactly as the bridge and as the gated-duplicate basis; all existing coefficient construction retained
study.proposed_difference: Replace only the fifth residual coefficient. From ten fixed block ranks r in [0,1], construct masked r^3 and fixed-permutation r^3. Two FP32 projection sweeps remove valid constants, the unscaled coarse linear coefficient and inherited fourth quadratic coefficient, with event-count weighting and recentering. Coefficients are block constant on valid events, hence also orthogonal to the centered within-block match and local-position directions in exact arithmetic. Common eligibility requires at least four occupied blocks, both new residual norm-squares >1e-10, nonzero incumbent fifth and local-position norm-squares >1e-10. Scale both new directions to the local-position coefficient norm; gated duplicate uses incumbent*eligibility and has that same norm. Bridge returns the exact incumbent coefficient ungated. All cells construct all alternatives and use the same five-channel contraction and adapters. No timestamps, sample identity, current action/labels, lookup, training change or new parameters. Rank is released array order, with no assumed elapsed-time interpretation. For exactly four occupied blocks the complement dimension is one, so ordered and scrambled residuals can be collinear; ordering attribution principally depends on histories occupying five or more blocks. Empty histories have zero residual corrections; learned shared parameters can still change their final predictions.
predictions: Predeclared primary: cubic_ordered exceeds cubic_scrambled, cubic_gated_duplicate and cubic_bridge on full-population validation is_click AUC. Only improvement over both source bests and the incumbent matters for predictive progress; exceeding a weakened replacement control alone is insufficient. The incumbent comparator is 0.6658605169646938; frozen source bests are 0.660646940486458 and 0.660163362657485.

Predeclared mechanism interpretation: ordered > scrambled and eligibility-matched duplicate supports usefulness of this coarse ordering beyond summary norm, input width and eligibility. Fixed learned capacity expected32129765 total/336549 dense; host must measure it. Same-seed bridge should reproduce incumbent scores exactly under deterministic execution. It is a parity/cost bridge, not independent repeated support.

Report click logloss and all four task AUC/logloss, auxiliary mean separately, full sample/positive/negative counts, allocated GPU and wall seconds, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 latency. Prefer no click-logloss worsening and inspect the observed auxiliary tradeoff. Same recipe isolates the coefficient; measured runtime is needed before any efficiency claim.

Use existing predeclared history bins 0,1-16,17-64,>64; negatives equal samples minus positives. History>64 is the principal exploratory ordering diagnostic, not a second selection score. Do not claim subgroup significance; new-eligibility and occupied-block diagnostics require an authorized host interface and may be unavailable. If admitted later, at least five occupied blocks is the predeclared noncollinearity diagnostic. User-cluster bootstrap and additional seeds are deferred until host resources/interfaces permit; a first-seed win remains preliminary.
falsifiers: Cubic failing to exceed the incumbent bridge, or either matched replacement control, rejects useful ordered-cubic replacement for this implementation under the fixed one-pass protocol. It does not refute every higher-order history representation.

If gated duplicate improves equally, availability/gating suffices as an alternative; if scrambled is as good as ordered, new generic projection/conditioning rather than cubic order remains the explanation. A small first-seed ranking is inconclusive without repetition.

Bridge disagreement with the incumbent, changed learned parameter counts, nonfinite outputs/gradients, padded-event sensitivity, unauthorized auxiliary item/scorer gradients or failed host forward/backward/BF16 checks invalidate the comparison before performance interpretation.
If added measured runtime erases a quality-cost advantage, do not claim efficiency. If click improves but auxiliary tasks regress, report the task tradeoff instead of unified four-task superiority.
alternative_explanations: Seed-specific optimization and adaptive validation selection across many earlier rounds; no held-out or repeated support exists here.
A support gate itself encodes match availability or history length; the eligibility-matched duplicate and exact bridge isolate this as far as this local comparison permits.

Normalization, coefficient distribution and optimizer conditioning remain different despite equal coefficient L2 norms and learned capacity; nonlinear adapters do not make the representations functionally equivalent.

Fixed padding/truncation and released array order can convey activity signatures rather than a causal temporal mechanism. Whole-window vocabulary and official_offline feedback assumptions remain inherited limitations.

The scrambled complement is sometimes collinear with the ordered complement, especially four-block histories, weakening the ordering contrast. BF16 coefficient quantization can also break exact algebraic orthogonality.

The common gate excludes histories with no within-block target-match contrast; this is a scoped replacement rather than a test of unconditional cubic information. Parameter learning transfers changes to ineligible histories, so slice differences cannot be attributed solely to direct access.
Primary-owned embeddings and scorer already reduce auxiliary quality relative to baseline; fixed ownership permits a click comparison but does not explain or fix that tradeoff.
